live_data_statements: All recruited participants were healthy, reported no history of psychiatric or neurological disorders, and were in no active medical treatment.

With respect to age, participants were divided into younger and older adults using a median split (at 25 years, younger adults: n = 50, mean age = 22.6 ± 2.0 years, range 18-25; older adults: n = 41, mean age = 34.3 ± 10.9 years, range .
When using the app, participants were prompted to pinpoint their symptoms on a 3D avatar integrated into the app that showed the body both from the inside and from the outside.

All participants provided written informed consent prior to participation and were compensated for their attendance (hourly rate of 8€ for the in-person interview, 12€ per weekly app assessment in addition to 14€ for app completion).
A total of N = 96 participants were recruited for the study (age = 27.
A total of N = 112 individuals were screened for eligibility, of these, n = 97 met inclusion criteria and were enrolled.

Of those, n = 6 participants were excluded from the analyses as n = 4 did not complete all 8 app rounds (one round missing in n = 3, two rounds missing in n = 1), and n = 2 had missing items in the paper-and-pencil-based questionnaires.

For example, the statement "I don't always know why I do what I do" was transferred to "I don't always know why my body reacts the way it does", assessing the degree to which participants are realistic about their ability to understand their own mental states (RFQ-8) or bodily states (BRFQ-9).
At the end of the in-person session, participants were familiarized with the app by one of 4 trained experimenters following a standardized, scripted protocol.
Participants were informed that they would get email and push notifications to remind them about the next round in case they enable this function in the app.
Participants were then asked to choose a starting date and it was recommended to start on a Sunday.
Participants were instructed to fill out the app once per week for the duration of 8 weeks, starting at their selected starting date.
When one round was missed (i.e., no data were submitted until midnight of the respective Sunday), participants were allowed to re-submit data on two consecutive weeks (i.e., + 7 days + 7 days).
Participants were given a maximum time of 10 weeks to complete 8 rounds.
If data of less than 8 rounds had arrived on the server 10 weeks after the selected starting date, participants were excluded from the analyses.
Participants were sent a standard reminder via an app notification and via email one day before the next round started.
Another set of n = 30 participants (26.67 years ± 4.18 years, range = 18-35 years) were recruited for validation purposes.
These participants completed the paper-and-pencilbased questionnaires at two time points, separated by 8-10 weeks, but without being enrolled in the app study (see more info below).
Participants were recruited between April 2024 and February 2025.

Overview experimental protocol. (a) Participants first completed paper-and-pencil-based questionnaires in an in-person interview. (b) Participants were then familiarized with the app Somascape that was installed on their own personal smartphones.
When first starting the app, participants were prompted to select their avatar. (c) Participants were asked to use the app once per week over an 8-week period, completing a total of 8 "rounds".
In the somatic module, participants were asked to localize their bodily symptoms on the 3D avatar, and to rate their intensity on a 1-100 scale.
